protocol_content.name: Immunotherapy (CAR-T) treatment for canine glioma tumors
protocol_content.tagline: Help us test CAR T cells and verdinexor, a new chemotherapy for gliomas in dogs.
protocol_content.description:
About 3 in 100 dogs are diagnosed with brain tumors each year, and gliomas are among the hardest to treat because they can escape traditional treatments. This study is focused on finding new treatment options for dogs with brain tumors, specifically gliomas, which are one of the most difficult types to treat. Researchers are exploring a new approach called immunotherapy, which helps the body’s own immune system fight cancer.


In this study, a small blood sample is taken from your dog to collect immune cells (called T cells). These cells are then modified in the lab to better recognize and attack cancer cells. The upgraded cells (called CAR T cells) are given back to your dog to target the tumor.


Dogs in this study will also receive a chemotherapy drug called verdinexor, which may help improve the effectiveness of the treatment.


Additionally, dogs can receive radiation therapy, which is currently the gold-standard for treating gliomas in dogs. We hope that by attacking the tumor through immunotherapy, radiation therapy, and chemotherapy, we will give dogs the best chance at success.


This is the first study to test this type of therapy in dogs, building on promising results seen in children with brain tumors.
protocol_content.requirements: A 5-month study period with frequent visitsInitial MRI (for eligibility)Blood collection to create CAR T cellsCAR T cell injections (two treatments)Radiation therapyBrain biopsy (case-dependent, not required)Follow-up MRI at month 1 and month 4 following initial CAR-T treatmentOngoing oral chemotherapy
protocol_content.responsibilities: Bring your dog to frequent visits at the Veterinary Health System facilitiesGive oral chemotherapy at home twice weeklyAllow your dog to undergo anesthesia for radiation therapy and potentially a brain biopsyComplete weekly electronic surveys
protocol_content.benefits: Benefits:Access to a cutting-edge, first-in-dogs treatmentStudy covers the cost of biopsy, treatments, and medications Study covers the cost of radiation therapy, which is currently the gold-standard for treating glioma tumorsChemotherapy costs covered for the rest of your dog’s lifeContribute to research that may improve cancer treatment for dogs and humansRisks:Risks associated with anesthesia, brain biopsy, and MRIPossible side effects from chemotherapy and immunotherapyFrequent visits and time commitmentTreatment may not be effective for some dogs
protocol_content.compensation: All study activities, including radiation therapy, recheck MRIs, all exams and bloodwork, and lifetime chemotherapy, are fully covered.
protocol_content.timeCommitment: Frequent visits over 5 months, which must be completed at CSU. During those 5 months, there will be chemotherapy administration at home, twice weekly.
